clue.text: Heated feeling — overdressed in fur wrap

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed in the middle of the word fur, which wraps them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dressed in the sense of arranged or prepared, so the letters of over are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clothes-mad person, hot under too much fur, gets passionately worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed' rearranges OVER into ERVO, and 'in' puts that inside FUR, which is the 'wrap'. 'overdressed' reads as one word but splits into fodder and indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour is intense passion or ardour, a hot emotional state.

clue.text: Beginner seen to sink

explanation.surface: A novice is seen to go under.
explanation.definitionFit: A founder is one who establishes something; also to founder is to fill with water and go down.

clue.text: Heading up a narrow passage to the right of the kidneys

indicators.note: Heading up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or passage

explanation.surface: Directions: go up the alley and turn right, near the kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading up' turns LANE into ENAL, placed to the right of R.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal is the adjective describing the kidneys.

clue.text: Don't be the first to drop the lids

definitions.text: Don't be the first to drop the lids

parts.words: Don't be the first to drop the lids
parts.note: eyelids are the lids; the one who keeps eyes open longest wins a gazing contest

explanation.surface: Advice for a staring contest: don't blink first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lids' seems to mean pan covers, but these are eyelids.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstare is to win a staring match by holding a gaze longer.

clue.text: Very special military combination

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army corps
RE is the Royal Engineers, another British army corps

explanation.surface: A rare alliance of military forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Artillery (RA) and Royal Engineers (RE) are British army corps, joined here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means uncommon and therefore exceptional or prized.

clue.text: No truce organised — defeat them utterly!

indicators.note: organised suggests the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A war cry: no ceasefire will be arranged, crush the enemy!
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the letters of NO TRUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is to beat them decisively in a contest.

clue.text: With wrought steel, manages to make these instruments

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the metal's letters are reshaped

parts.note: to manage is to cope

explanation.surface: Worked steel is used to make optical instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrought' rearranges STEEL into TELES, then COPES follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Telescopes are optical instruments for viewing distant objects.

clue.text: Compensate for not being on deposit

parts.note: something not on is off
to set down is to deposit

explanation.surface: Making up for a deposit not being paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset is to counterbalance one thing against another.

clue.text: Near-wrecked flat and left after sunset

parts.note: nigh is an old word for near

indicators.note: wrecked means smashed up, so the letters of flat are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ruined apartment abandoned at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges FLAT into TFAL, between NIGH and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the onset of darkness that follows sunset.

clue.text: Writer with snub-nose grabs me, encountering resistance

indicators.note: grabs means the turned word holds the other pieces inside
a snub nose turns up, so in a down clue the word nose is turned upward

parts.note: taken as written
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An author with a turned-up nose meets opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snub' turns NOSE into ESON, and 'grabs' puts ME and R inside it. Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and poet.

clue.text: Affected by frantic annual

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Affected by frantic annual' with no count: ANNUAL anagrammed gives only six of nine letters (U, R, T missing), so the clue is cut short and no source gives the rest.

clue.text: Few, they say, get unduly tec initially, playing it?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Few, they say, get unduly tec initially, playing it?': FU (sounding like few) plus initials needs G, U, E, but 'tec' gives T; the OCR word is garbled and no source gives the printed word.
annotationWithheld.clue: Few, they say, get unduly tec initially, playing it?

clue.text: In the river, permitted to strike out

indicators.note: In tells us one piece is put inside the river named

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in England and Wales
permitted means let, as in allowed

explanation.surface: Someone is allowed to cast a line from the river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts LET inside DEE, a British river that crosswords use often.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete text is to cross it out or remove it.

clue.text: Animal wisest to duck inside for fire protection

indicators.note: inside places the following pieces within the animal's name

parts.note: the donkey or ass is an animal
the wisest is the best, the top choice
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to a clever creature: get your head down if there's a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts BEST and O into ASS. A duck is a zero score in cricket, the British bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a mineral fibre once used widely for fireproofing.

clue.text: After smashing of the atom, entire globe has had to suffer its pollution

definitions.text: After smashing of the atom, entire globe has had to suffer its pollution

indicators.note: smashing breaks the word atom into a new arrangement

parts.note: a globe is a sphere

explanation.surface: After nuclear fission, the whole world suffers air pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' rearranges ATOM into ATMO, and SPHERE follows; the whole clue describes polluted air.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere is the air envelope of the Earth, which fallout pollutes.

clue.text: Traveller getting a share of the compensation

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
a ration is one's allotted share

explanation.surface: A salesman takes his cut of a payout.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparation is making amends, payment given for a wrong or damage.

clue.text: Gets inside with mate and peers around

indicators.note: around means the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks in with a friend while onlookers gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges MATE and PEERS together.
explanation.definitionFit: To permeate is to spread through or penetrate something.

clue.text: Lend uncle one piece

explanation.surface: Lend your uncle one piece of the set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker, so to pawn is to hand goods to uncle for a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawning means leaving goods with a pawnbroker for cash; also a pawn is a single chessman of the lowest rank.

clue.text: Converse with mate on location

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or mate
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Chat with your partner on site.
explanation.walkthrough: OPPO is British informal for a pal or counterpart. 'Converse' looks like a verb (talk), but is the noun meaning reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The converse is the reverse or contrary of something.

clue.text: Reportedly a banned poet

indicators.note: Reportedly means as heard spoken, so a word sounding like barred is wanted

parts.note: banned means barred, prohibited

explanation.surface: A poet whose work has been banned, so they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals that the word for banned is heard, not written.
explanation.definitionFit: A bard is a poet, especially an epic or lyric one; Shakespeare is the Bard.

clue.text: Scientists finding what's putrefied in rubbish containers

indicators.note: in means one piece sits within the containers

parts.note: bins hold rubbish
food that has gone bad is off

explanation.surface: Researchers find rotten food in the waste bins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OFF inside BINS. Boffins is British slang for scientists.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is British informal for a scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: Have a passion for fruit and tomatoes

parts.note: to have a passion for something is to love it
apples are a fruit

explanation.surface: A fruit lover's enthusiasm extends to tomatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Love apple is an old name for the tomato.
explanation.definitionFit: Love apple is an archaic name for the tomato, once thought an aphrodisiac.

clue.text: Compilers going to the dogs

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers are going to the dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters are breeds of gun dog; 'going to the' links, and the idiom 'going to the dogs' disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword compilers are called setters; also setters are gundogs such as the Irish breed.

clue.text: Formerly in Greece, young men the last to be hip, perhaps

indicators.note: the last means the final letter of the word the
perhaps hints the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: In ancient Greece, the young were the last to be fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the last' gives E, and 'perhaps' rearranges BE and HIP into PHEBI.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephebi were young men in ancient Greece undergoing civic and military training.

clue.text: Charge of the French trapping young Philip in the tube

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: trapping means the French word holds the young man's name within it

parts.note: de is French for of
Pip is a pet name for Philip, as in Great Expectations

explanation.surface: A French fine is levied on a boy caught on the Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapping' puts PIP inside DE. 'the tube' tempts us toward the London Underground, but it is simply a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A feed pipe is a conduit carrying supply, such as water to a boiler.

clue.text: Cat gets bird — another bird gets both

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A cat catches a bird, and another bird ends up with both.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer joins the male cat to the second bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomtit is a familiar name for small titmice such as the blue tit.

clue.text: Spruce up the vehicles

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: spruce means smart, neat in appearance

explanation.surface: Smarten up the vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SMART around. 'Spruce up' looks like one phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are rail vehicles running on street tracks.

clue.text: After second time round, parking — as per instruction

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: After going round a second time, park as directed.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop is a command to halt, an order printed on signs.

clue.text: Fibre that after weaving, can be used in textiles

definitions.text: Fibre that after weaving, can be used in textiles

parts.words: Fibre that after weaving, can be used in textiles
parts.note: a plant fibre described plainly, while the letters of the last word, rearranged, nearly hold it

explanation.surface: A fibre that is woven into cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Its letters can be found by rearranging part of 'textiles', a teasing hint.
explanation.definitionFit: Ixtle is a strong Mexican agave fibre used for cord, brushes and coarse cloth.

clue.text: Trace exit — eccentric way to get out

indicators.note: eccentric way means an odd arrangement of the given letters

explanation.surface: Find the way out by an odd route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric way' rearranges TRACE EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free or disentangle oneself from difficulty.

clue.text: The poetic yearn for surprise development, with romance initially spurned

indicators.note: development suggests the remaining letters grow into a new form
spurned means rejected, so a letter is removed
initially picks the first letter of the word romance

explanation.surface: A poet longs for a surprise twist even when love is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from romance; 'spurned' removes it from SURPRISE, leaving SUPRISE, and 'development' rearranges that. 'The poetic' marks a literary word.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspire is a poetic word meaning to sigh or long for something.

clue.text: Less pea soup satisfies

indicators.note: soup suggests the letters mixed into a broth, rearranged

explanation.surface: Thin pea soup still hits the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soup' rearranges LESS PEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to satisfy or gratify them.
